A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe TRINITY: An Evolved LLM Coordinator. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A.1–A.7 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, optimizer comparisons and representation analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark scores, ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The coordinator backbone, lightweight head, singular-value fine-tuning, tri-role protocol and sep-CMA-ES training remain unchanged. Figure 2's shortened caption does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MATH500, MMLU, RLPR and LiveCodeBench, plus held-out AIME2025, BigCodeBench, MT-Bench and GPQA-D evaluations. Appendix dataset coverage and synthetic separability scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same individual-model variants, MasRouter, RouterDC, Smoothie, MoA, random selection, Majority@5 and prompted Gemini coordinator. Table 4 retains REINFORCE, SFT and random search.

E3.justification: Both specify LiveCodeBench V1 training with 400 samples and V6 testing with 175 samples, default 4096-token outputs and five coordination turns. Extended-budget evaluations and appendix experimental protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component and fixed-agent ablations in Table 2, head comparisons in Table 3, turn-budget sensitivity, agent-distribution analyses and Appendix A.3 separability studies are retained without substantive revision.

E5.justification: Reported seed/run information and uncertainty practices remain the same, including three-seed SFT label generation in Appendix A.2, the LiveCodeBench uncertainty reported in the introduction and Table 7's uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main-text and appendix result entries, numerical values and findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains TRINITY's 54.21 average, and Figure 4 and Section 4.4 retain the 0.862 LiveCodeBench pass@1 result.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 retains the same definitions, assumptions, propositions and proofs. The head equations in Appendix A.4 and dataset–agent selection formulation in Appendix A.6 are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight coordination, training efficiency, benchmark performance and generalization. Replacing 'amazing' with 'substantial' in Section 4.4 does not alter scientific claim scope.

C2.justification: Both retain the same explanations connecting separability and coordination to performance, interpretations of baseline weaknesses, and limitations. Section 6's distinction between planning tool use and actually executing tools is unchanged.

D1.justification: Backbone and head specifications, parameter counts, SFT hyperparameters, optimizer and baseline settings, and the statement promising supplementary source code and trained weights remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to model merging, routing and multi-agent scaffolding.

P1.justification: v2 shortens Figure 2's caption and replaces 'amazing' with 'substantial.' The author-contribution paragraph revises Qi Sun's role to leading training and evaluation and removes Peter Schwendeman's individual contribution sentence. Most prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 changes the highlighted token from blue to gray and the 'Head Input' label from blue to black, with a shorter caption. Conference headers and local reflow alter page layout; no figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 mainly updates publication formatting, author-contribution prose and Figure 2's styling and caption. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, theory and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These limited editorial adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
